stories.headline: Karnataka seeks ₹7,143 crore Central aid for drought relief
stories.title: Karnataka seeks ₹7,143 crore Central aid for drought relief
stories.summary: Shivakumar holds discussions with the Centre’s Inter-Ministerial Central Team, which is visiting Karnataka to assess drought situation and crop loss
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Karnataka government has sought ₹7,142.64 crore in financial assistance from the Centre for drought relief and mitigation measures following crop losses during the 2026 kharif season.
The State had initially sought ₹3,705.30 crore for 101 drought-affected taluks.
It subsequently submitted a supplementary memorandum seeking an additional ₹3,437.34 crore after another 76 taluks were declared drought-affected, taking the total to 177 taluks.
Ground verification is under way in 40 more taluks, which are also likely to be declared drought-affected.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday held discussions with the Centre’s Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT), which is visiting Karnataka to assess the drought situation and crop losses.
The State presented details of the damage and its financial requirements and submitted the memorandums to the team, which is scheduled to conduct on-the-spot assessments in the affected areas.
According to the memorandums, the estimated drought-related losses across the 177 affected taluks stand at ₹46,324.50 crore.
The State has sought ₹7,142.64 crore from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) for relief and mitigation measures.

The first memorandum, covering 101 taluks, sought ₹3,705.30 crore, including ₹2,017.26 crore for agriculture, ₹583.04 crore for animal husbandry, ₹805 crore for drinking water supply, and ₹300 crore towards gratuitous relief.
The estimated losses in these taluks were pegged at ₹18,748.23 crore.
The supplementary memorandum covering the additional 76 taluks seeks ₹3,437.34 crore, comprising ₹2,981.34 crore towards agricultural input subsidy and ₹456 crore for drinking water supply.
The estimated losses in these taluks stand at ₹27,576.22 crore.

stories.headline: Sanctions, tariffs turn into policy instruments, sometimes weaponised: P K Mishra
stories.title: Sanctions, tariffs turn into policy instruments, sometimes weaponised: P K Mishra
stories.summary: P K Mishra said India is a major energy importer, and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Principal Secretary to the prime minister, P K Mishra, on Saturday said export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy and they are sometimes even weaponised.
The top government functionary also said that wars disrupt energy and food markets while shipping routes and geographical choke points become sources of economic vulnerability.

Addressing the Kautilya Economic Conclave on the subject 'A World Priced for Risk', he said India is a major energy importer, and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely.
India's response, therefore, has combined several layers of protection.
"For energy security, the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has been a particularly clear reminder of how geography can translate into economic risk," he said.
Without mentioning any country, the top official said export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy, sometimes they are even weaponised.
The United States has in the past announced tariffs on a number of countries, including India, for a variety of reasons.

Recently, the US has enacted the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises tariffs of up to 100 per cent on nations purchasing Russian oil and gas, including India and China.
Mishra said India has maintained substantial stocks, increased domestic production where possible, diversified procurement, and ensured that alternative supply routes and suppliers are available.
For example, he said, the number of countries from which India imports crude oil has increased from 27 to 43, which is "very large".
"The same logic applies to energy transition.

Greater domestic capacity in renewables, nuclear energy, storage and associated technologies is not only about sustainability, it is also about reducing exposure to external shocks over time," he said.

stories.headline: Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh pitches ‘team spirit’ to faction-ridden unit
stories.title: Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh pitches ‘team spirit’ to faction-ridden unit
stories.summary: Newly appointed PCC chief reaches out to competing factions amid the upcoming Assembly election; appeals to all those who left Congress to return to the party
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amid deep factionalism in the Punjab Congress and ahead of the Assembly election, newly appointed Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief Pargat Singh on Saturday (October 3, 2026) drew on his experience as former captain of the Indian hockey team, and stressed the importance of team spirit and being a team player.
Replacing Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who headed the party’s Punjab unit for more than four years, Mr. Singh repeatedly used the language of sport to underline his approach to the job.
“I have been a team player,” he told reporters here, adding that he had always played as a “full-back” — a position centred on supporting the team from behind.
“I feel there are very good players in our team.
We will take all decisions unanimously,” he said, in a clear attempt to reach out to the party’s competing factions and senior leaders.
He recast the gaze from internal differences to the larger political context in Punjab.
“The issue is Punjab and not differences amongst us,” he said, while describing Mr. Warring as a “player of our team”.
He also said that all the senior leaders would be ahead of him in the team.
“We are a team.
This is Rahul Gandhi’s team,” Mr. Singh said, adding that the Congress would pursue “constructive politics” and seek to “revive democracy”.

His emphasis on cohesion comes at a politically difficult moment for the Punjab Congress, which has been marked by factional differences as the party prepares for the Assembly election, due early next year.

Mr. Singh, who called on the All India Congress Committee general secretary in-charge of Punjab, Sachin Pilot, stressed on building a “very good team in Punjab” and gave a call to those who had left the Congress to return if they wanted to contribute to the State.

stories.headline: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
stories.title: Missing Deadline Behind Punjab's Chief Justice Dispute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, notified on 5 September 2026, has drawn an unusually public objection from the State of Punjab, whose Cabinet resolved the next day that the appointment had been made without the State's consent.
The real question, however, is not whether Punjab's consent was required, for it plainly was not.
It is whether a State that has been asked for its views, and has not given them, can be said to have been consulted when the rules prescribe no time within which it must answer.
That question arises because the Memorandum of Procedure treats the two kinds of High Court appointment differently.
Where the Chief Justice of a High Court proposes a new judge, the State Government has six weeks to comment.
If it does not reply, paragraph 14 permits the Union to presume that the Governor, that is, the Chief Minister, “has nothing to add”, and to proceed.
Where the appointment is of the Chief Justice, paragraph 6 prescribes no period at all.

It is submitted that this gap, rather than the conduct of either party, lies at the heart of the dispute, and that it can be closed by a single amendment to a document the Government has been expected to revise since 2015.
The Collegium recommended Justice Mishra on 6 August 2026, and the Law Ministry sought Punjab's views between 10 and 12 August.
Haryana, which shares the High Court, responded, as did the Governors of both States; Punjab's elected government did not.
The Union notified the appointment on 5 September together with seven others, and the Chief Minister stayed away from the oath two days later.

The Additional Solicitor General has since maintained that a week or two was ample time for the State to respond, while Punjab's own Cabinet has acknowledged that no time limit is prescribed for the appointment of a Chief Justice.

stories.headline: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to defend Asian Games hockey gold, seal LA Olympics berth
stories.title: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to defend Asian Games hockey gold, seal LA Olympics berth
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to retain the Asian Games hockey gold and secure direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Kakamigahara: India defeated Malaysia 5-1 in the men's hockey final at the Asian Games on Saturday to retain their gold medal and secure direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The victory marked India's fifth Asian Games gold in men's hockey and their second consecutive title.
It was also the first time India had successfully defended the men's hockey gold at the Asian Games.
Captain Harmanpreet Singh led the scoring with two goals, converting penalty corners in the 11th and 57th minutes.
Jugraj Singh added another penalty-corner goal in the 23rd minute.
Vice-captain Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke in the 42nd minute, while Shilanand Lakra completed India's tally with a field goal in the 54th minute.
Malaysia's only goal came in the 14th minute through Shello Silverius, who scored from a field effort.
India dominated possession and territory early in the match, spending much of the opening quarter in the Malaysian half.
Malaysia settled for the silver medal, while Pakistan claimed bronze after defeating South Korea 5-3 earlier on Saturday.
The men's team's triumph came a day after India's women's team also won Asian Games gold.
The women defeated defending champions and reigning Olympic silver medallists China 1-0 on Friday to claim the title after a 44-year wait.
